summary: The doctor path without a practice licence. A signed-in account chooses the doctor path, or opens the claim page of a published unowned directory profile, and applies with its name, general or specialist (required; NOT_DECLARED is never a choice), a council code normalised as in Phase 2 and a council card; no licence document is accepted on this path. The application is a COUNCIL professional case with an immutable version-1 submission that records declaredLicence false, created under an account row lock. It is refused for an account with any other open professional case, an open Phase 2 application, a doctor or student profile, a tag or the TRUSTED_VET role, and for a council code another profile holds; when that profile is an unowned published page the refusal carries its claim address. A claim may only target a published, unowned, unmerged page, must match the page's council code if it has one, and only one claim of a page may be open. The association admin (ASSOCIATION_OPERATOR or SUPERADMIN, DEC-0190) verifies the council code by hand, asks for a correction or rejects, always with a reason, never on their own case and never on a stale version; a correction is answered with a new submission version while the earlier one stays. Verification rechecks everything, then either creates the doctor's profile or transfers the claimed page with a conditional update that only succeeds while the page is still unowned, so an owned record can never be taken over and a failed transfer rolls the whole approval back. The profile becomes DOCTOR with the declared scope, a verified council code with its verifier and has_licence false; the case becomes VERIFIED_NO_LICENSE; and exactly the unlicensed doctor tag with that scope is given. No role, licence code or licence verification, Finder place or trusted eligibility follows, while directory introduction does: the verified doctor writes, locates and publishes the page. A later licence case can open beside the closed council case and add licence data and a new tag while the council submissions, the council case status and the unlicensed tag row stay. The Phase 2 submission action and form were removed, so every new doctor application goes to the association; applications already open in Phase 2 finish in /review/vets, and their mirrored cases are not decidable from the association queue. The association has a queue with open, correction and decided views, a detail page with every version, the documents, the claimed page, the same council code elsewhere and the history, a count on its overview and a navigation entry; the applicant sees status, reasons, documents and history on the account page and can answer a correction there.

limitations: The Phase 2 service function that creates an application remains in code for applications already open and for its tests; it has no product entry point any more.
One open claim per page is enforced by the service, not by a database index; two claims cannot both be approved because the transfer is conditional.
A verified doctor cannot change general/specialist yet, and Phase 2 doctors with NOT_DECLARED have no declaration path in this prompt.
The new doctor path has no appeal after rejection and no applicant withdrawal; a new application may follow a rejection.
The real licence flow is PROMPT-006; the upgrade is proven at the data level only.
Deciding a submitted case performs the start of review and the decision in one step; claiming a case is PROMPT-007.
The tag label uses the hyphenated form of PHASE_2_5_SPEC_FA §3, while the prompt text writes it with em dashes.
The full 161-test browser matrix was not rerun; eight suites passing through the changed code were.
Screenshots were taken only inside the temporary worktree and are not committed; visual fidelity of the new pages is unverified.
